title: Subarcsecond Imaging of the Complex Organic Chemistry in Massive Star-forming Region G10.6-0.4
question: How is the complex organic molecule (COM) chemistry of the massive star-forming region G10.6-0.4 spatially structured on small scales, and what do the resolved temperature, column density and correlation maps say about COM formation?

evidence.quote: at a distance of 4.95 kpc (cite: Sanna14)

what.value: Expected 12C/13C ratio of 43 at Galactocentric distance 3.9 kpc

evidence.quote: This is a factor of two lower than the expected ratio of 43 (cite: Milam05)

evidence.loc: Rotational Temperature and Column Density Derivation
evidence.quote: we used the complete rotational-torsional-vibrational partition function from (cite: Carvajal19).

what.value: Literature COM column densities and abundances of other massive young stellar objects, used for comparison

evidence.quote: we compared them against spatially-resolved data from: AFGL 4176 (cite: Bogelund19); G34.26 (cite: Mookerjea07);

external_data.citation: Bogelund19, Mookerjea07, Allen17, Guzman18, Feng16, Bonfand17, Bonfand19, Molet19 (as cited in the paper)

what.value: Typical MYSO CH3OCH3/CH3OH ratio of 14%, and CH3CHO/CH3OH trends in resolved vs unresolved MYSOs

evidence.quote: Compared to the typical MYSOs ratios of 14% from (cite: Oberg_Faraday)

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image the line cubes
recipe.method: Calibration by ALMA/NAASC staff, then imaging of data cubes with tclean using Briggs robust 0.5
key_parameters: robust = 0.5; 0.018 arcsec pixels; cubes trimmed to inner 9 x 7 arcsec

recipe.goal: Subtract continuum in the image plane
recipe.method: Per-pixel continuum level from the distribution of channel intensities, following Jorgensen et al. 2016
key_parameters: Symmetric Gaussian fit to each pixel's flux density distribution, then a skewed Gaussian over a range defined by that centroid; the new centroid is the continuum level

recipe.goal: Measure continuum rms per spectral window
recipe.method: Median over pixels without significant continuum emission, excluding the central 0.06 pc region and the western UC HII region

recipe.goal: Fit line profiles pixel by pixel
recipe.method: Single Gaussian fits to all unblended transitions of each species, with a template line per species setting limits for the other lines
key_parameters: Pixel mask at 5 sigma peak intensity within a 10 km/s window around each transition
Initial template fits: FWHM allowed 1.3 to 15 km/s

recipe.goal: Derive rotational temperature and column density maps
recipe.method: Pixel-by-pixel rotational diagram with optical depth correction, posterior sampled with emcee
key_parameters: Initial parameter space 1e14-1e20 cm^-2 and 10-800 K, then a second iteration with narrower species-specific grids
Partition functions linearly interpolated from catalog values (JPL, CDMS)
Reported values are the 50th, 16th and 84th percentiles of the marginalized posteriors
assumptions: LTE level populations; optical depth correction factor applied; solid angle set by the 0.018 arcsec pixel

recipe.method: CH3OCHO uses CH3OH temperature; CH3CH2CN fit with two temperature components where warranted; optically thick CH3CN replaced by CH3 13CN scaled by a 12C/13C ratio from CH3OH/13CH3OH
key_parameters: Median CH3OH/13CH3OH column density ratio of 22.8 adopted as 12C/13C
assumptions: 13CH3OH uses the CH3OH rotational temperature; HC1 excluded when deriving 13CH3OH column densities

recipe.method: Cross-correlation coefficient between column density maps sampled on a common quarter-beam grid, with and without masking HC1; scatter plots of N vs N and N vs T
key_parameters: CH2CHCN excluded from the cross-correlation for lack of independent points
assumptions: No fractional abundances relative to H2; column densities compared directly

recipe.goal: Compare hot cores with literature sources
recipe.method: Compare HC1 and HC2 fractional abundances and column density ratios with literature MYSOs, Galactic center clouds, comets and low-mass YSOs

evidence.loc: Data Reduction, Continuum Subtraction, and Imaging
evidence.quote: Overall, we found a typical continuum rms of ${\sim}0.60$–$0.65$ mJy beam$^{-1}$ (${\sim}0.79$–$0.87$ K)
Overall, we find a median column density ratio of 22.8, which is the value we adopt.

answer_key.quantity: CH3CH2CN primary (cold) component temperature at HC1
CH3CH2CN secondary (hot) component temperature at HC1
Nearly constant CH3OCH3/CH3OH column density ratio

evidence.quote: we identify a nearly constant ratio of CH$_3$OCH$_3$ with respect to CH$_3$OH of 2%

answer_key.quantity: Pearson correlation coefficient, HNCO vs NH2CHO column density

evidence.quote: This correlation is strong with a Pearson’s correlation coefficient of $r=0.87$

answer_key.quantity: Power law relating N(NH2CHO) to N(HNCO)

evidence.quote: It is well-characterized by a single power law given by \[N$_{\rm{NH}{_2}\rm{CHO}}] = 0.01 \times [\rm{N}_{\rm{HNCO}}]^{1.09}$.

answer_key.quantity: CH2CHCN/CH3CH2CN column density ratio at HC1 and HC2

evidence.quote: We find CH$_2$CHCN/CH$_3$CH$_2$CN ratios of 0.49$\pm$0.30 and 0.23$\pm$0.04 for HC1 and HC2, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Highest cross-correlation (CH2CHCN/HNCO) and its pixel overlap

evidence.quote: A good example of this is the correlation between CH$_2$CHCN/HNCO, which is the highest correlation observed (0.95), but only has a 7% pixel overlap.
